A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAGGED study. Their text, tables, figures, and complete appendices—A–B in v1 and A–D in v2—support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original retrieval and reader evaluations on NQ, HotpotQA, and BioASQ, including context-quantity and gold/non-gold passage analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original results on the same datasets, retaining and expanding the reader comparisons and robustness analyses.

M1.justification: RAGGED retains its retriever–reader pipeline, QA prompt, and analysis axes: component choice, context quantity, and gold-passage data slices. Additional reader models are evaluated within this framework; no new algorithmic component or training objective is introduced.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate English NQ, HotpotQA, and BioASQ using the same Wikipedia and PubMed corpora. Single-hop, multi-hop, biomedical, and gold/non-gold context scenarios are retained. Appendix B preserves the dataset sizes and splits.

E2.justification: v2 adds GPT-3.5-turbo, Claude Haiku, Llama3 8B, and Llama3 70B to the existing FLAN-T5, FLAN-UL2, and two Llama2 readers. These participate in the reported comparisons and robustness plots. BM25 and ColBERT remain the compared retrievers.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 replaces exact match with F1 for NQ. Section 2.2 changes the reported k sampling grid from {1,2,3,5,10,20,30} to {1,2,5,10,20,50}. Appendix A changes the stated output lengths from 10 and 256 tokens to 10 tokens only. These are reported protocol revisions, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The retained gold/non-gold robustness analyses are substantially expanded across the additional readers, including Appendix D. v2 replaces the FLAN-T5 conditional same-page case study with a cross-model accuracy comparison and adds observations of gibberish responses from Claude Haiku and Llama3 70B under gold biomedical contexts.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance-testing procedures. Both describe greedy decoding without adding uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive reader results and revises existing curves. BM25 paragraph recall@50 changes from 7.5 to 22.8 on NQ and from 3.0 to 54.2 on HotpotQA (v1 Table 2; v2 Table 3), while corresponding page-recall and ColBERT rows remain unchanged. NQ reader scores now use F1, so their increases cannot be interpreted as same-metric performance gains.

T1.justification: Neither version contains substantive theoretical results, formal assumptions, or proofs. The retained framework uses elementary indexing and standard metrics; the scoring changes do not introduce new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction replace v1's broad encoder-decoder versus decoder-only claims about context use and memorization with model-specific noise-robustness findings. Figure 2 now groups FLAN/GPT versus Llama/Claude by observed behavior. The central contribution of a reusable configuration-analysis framework is retained.

C2.justification: Sections 5–6 substantially revise the explanations of reader behavior. v2 introduces multiple supporting passages as possible anchors against noise, biomedical terminology as a possible filtering aid, and explicit gibberish failure conditions. These replace or extend v1's emphasis on memorization conflicts and model size. The limitations paragraph is unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds Llama3 tokenization/truncation details, configurations for the additional readers, and approximately $300 in closed-model expenditure. Appendix B and Table 3 clarify PubMed passage and retrieval units. Existing hardware, batching, dataset licenses, and code/data access information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Brown et al. (2020) and Enis and Hopkins (2024), replaces the original ColBERT citation with Santhanam et al.'s ColBERTv2 reference, and removes Richardson et al. (2013). Section 8's substantive positioning against prior research remains essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, framework explanations, and Sections 5–7 are extensively rewritten. No-context evaluation moves from Section 6 to Section 5, Section 6 is reorganized around gold-passage presence, and retriever discussion is consolidated. Appendices C–D reorganize supporting material.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn, and the empirical figures receive expanded model legends and reorganized panels. The separate no-context table disappears while Figure 3 includes k=0 results. The retrieval table moves to Appendix C, and Appendix D redisplays and expands the gold/non-gold plots.

improvement.justification: The decisive improvement is replacing architecture-wide conclusions drawn from two model families with model-specific guidance supported by broader comparisons and robustness evidence (Abstract; Sections 5–6). This substantially strengthens the paper's main practical takeaway. Reporting weaknesses remain: the BM25 score revisions are unexplained, and Section 6.1's Llama2 threshold statement conflicts with Figure 4, limiting confidence in some detailed numerical claims.
